description: Deterministic plugin runtime with LLM-judgment dispatch and side-effect approval gates. Plugins declare their side effects; declared effects require human session approval at every autonomy level. Judgment work is handed off via the [needs-llm] contract rather than the plugin calling a model.
rules: A plugin is a manifest plus a handler. The manifest is a declaration of capability that the runtime enforces, not documentation.

A non-empty side_effects array gates execution behind session approval at EVERY autonomy level, autonomous included. autonomy_level describes how a plugin is scheduled, never what it is permitted to touch.
An unapproved side-effecting plugin is recorded as skipped and the run continues. It is not an error and it does not halt the pipeline.
Plugins never call an LLM. Judgment work is emitted as a [needs-llm] handoff, which maps to the delegated run status and is never retried.

Generated plugin code imports siblings with an explicit .ts extension. Node's type stripping resolves the literal specifier; a .js specifier at a .ts file is ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND under Node, and Bun hides this by remapping.
Manifests are validated with .parse(), not .safeParse(). An invalid manifest is a hard stop at load — a misconfigured plugin never silently runs.
Manifest top level must stay declarative: no I/O, no side effects. Importing a manifest executes its module top level, and that happens during warpline plan, before any approval gate.
